key_insight: Microalgae can be captured in sea-spray jet droplets through jet hydrodynamics, revealing a potential particulate pathway for airborne algal toxins.
engineering_relevance: Hydrodynamic capture models could improve predictions of biological particle transfer from seawater into coastal aerosols.
method: Examine microalgal capture in droplets produced by bursting bubbles across multiple species.
Measure enrichment in the first jet drop relative to the bulk liquid.
Develop a capture model based on particle dynamics within the jet rather than surface effects.
evidence_signal: The study reports consistent microalgal capture, two enrichment regimes with a strongly cell-size-dependent transition, and aerosolization of toxic Ostreopsis cf. ovata cells.
watch_item: The relative contribution of cell-associated versus dissolved toxins to airborne exposure remains unresolved.
paper_title: Hydrodynamics of microalgae in sea spray
